messages:
sam: Hey team — seeing intermittent 504s from Go SDK streaming responses after I tweaked transport keepalives in dev. Repro steps below, pinging @emily @vikram :thinking:

emily: ugh, timeline? pushed keepalive change today?
sam: pushed ~10:12 UTC. symptoms: client stalls mid-stream, ctx cancel doesn't close stream; server logs keep the stream open until timeout. small payloads fine, big ones fail more.
vikram: can you paste transport config and minimal req code?
sam: sure:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  DisableKeepAlives: false,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", url, nil)
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```
sam: then we read resp.Body via io.Copy to stream
emily: does canceling the ctx call `resp.Body.Close()`? have you tried `client.CloseIdleConnections()` on cancel?
sam: yes we call `resp.Body.Close()` in defer in reader goroutine. cancel doesn't seem to unblock the server side.
vikram: suspicious of http2 stream reuse + connection pooling. try setting `ForceAttemptHTTP2: true`? also temp test: set `DisableKeepAlives: true` to see if problem goes away.
emily: also try lowering `IdleConnTimeout` to 5s and `MaxIdleConnsPerHost` to 2 to force less reuse — see if issue reproduces.
sam: quick test results: DisableKeepAlives = true => no 504s in 20 runs. with keepalives true => 6/20 504s.
vikram: ok that points to conn reuse. probably streams not being fully torn down on ctx cancel. Could be our client code not draining body before Close. When using http2 you must Read until EOF or Close — but Close should be enough. Try explicit `io.Copy(ioutil.Discard, resp.Body)` before Close.
emily: also check if middleware wraps ctx and strips cancel propagation. Are you creating child contexts with `context.WithTimeout` and not passing that into request?
sam: we pass the ctx returned by our handler; yes. sample shows `req.WithContext(ctx)`.
vikram: last idea: enable keepalive probe TTL on dialer to detect dead peers faster. sample dialer:
```go
netDialer := &net.Dialer{KeepAlive: 15 * time.Second, Timeout: 10 * time.Second}
tr.DialContext = netDialer.DialContext
```
sam: thanks — i'll run tests with DisableKeepAlives=false + explicit drain + Dialer keepalive + lower idle timeout and report back.
ops-bot: dev rolling-restart started for inference-dev cluster (job/streaming-repro) — ETA 3m
sam: done testing — disabling keepalives fixed it, draining + dialer keepalives reduced failures to 0/50. i'll open a short PR with `resp.Body` draining in streaming path and add a transport tuning doc in the repo.
emily: awesome, pls add a note about potential http2 caveat in README. thx :thumbsup: 
vikram: file an issue to track if this is go net/http http2 bug or our assumptions; tag me.
sam: created issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/4821 — assigned to @vikram
